name: Lisbon
description: Tram rides, pastel streets, riverside light, and evenings of fado and fresh seafood.
heroDescription: Spread across seven hills above the Tagus, Lisbon is a city of tiled facades, creaking trams, and long, golden afternoons. Wander at an easy pace and let the viewpoints find you.

intro.title: Getting to Lisbon
intro.text: Lisbon is well connected, with most travellers arriving by air. The airport is close to the centre, which makes the first afternoon easy.

routes.name: Lisbon Airport (LIS)
routes.text: About 20-30 minutes to the centre by metro (Red then Green line) or AeroBus.

routes.name: From Porto
routes.text: Roughly 2.5-3 hours by intercity train from Campanhã to Lisboa-Oriente.

routes.name: From the Algarve
routes.text: Around 4 hours by train; check seasonal services and connections.

itineraryTitle: A loose three-day wander through the city, with time for viewpoints and long dinners.

days.title: Alfama & the old quarter
days.text: Lose yourself in tiled lanes and listen for fado drifting from open doorways. This is the Lisbon of postcards, best on foot and unhurried.
bullets: Ride the historic Tram 28 through Alfama and Graça early to beat the crowds.
Climb to Miradouro de Santa Luzia for rooftops and river light.
End with a fado dinner in a small tasca.

images.alt: Yellow tram on a Lisbon street

days.title: Belém & the river
days.text: Head west along the Tagus to where the Age of Discovery began. Wide esplanades, grand monuments, and the original pastel de nata.
bullets: See the Jerónimos Monastery and the Belém Tower (book ahead in season).
Try a warm pastel de nata at the original Pastéis de Belém.
Walk the riverside promenade back towards the city as the light softens.

days.title: Chiado, Bairro Alto & sunset
days.text: A slower final day of bookshops, cafes, and the city's famous viewpoints, finishing with a sunset drink over the rooftops.
bullets: Browse Livraria Bertrand (claimed to be the world's oldest bookshop) in Chiado.
Ride the Elevador de Santa Justa or the Gloria funicular up to Bairro Alto.
Catch sunset from Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara, then find dinner.

food.title: Pastéis de nata
food.text: Warm custard tarts, best with a bica (espresso).

food.title: Tasca petiscos
food.text: Small plates of bacalhau, grilled sardines, olives, and cheese.

food.title: Ginja
food.text: A sweet cherry liqueur, often sipped from a chocolate cup in Alcântara or Rossio.

tip.title: Travlzi tip: ride the trams off-peak
tip.text: Tram 28 fills up by mid-morning. Ride early or late, buy a Viva Viagem pass for the day, and wear comfortable shoes for those hills.
